title: Lower your wing
hookLine: lower your wing to the believers who follow you (26:215)

lines: A HEN SPREADS HER WINGS LOW.
A RAISED WING, A LOWERED WING.
THE SURAH TURNS TO THE PROPHET.
cards: Watch a hen when the sky darkens. She doesn't make a speech. She crouches, spreads her wings low, and the chicks run under.
A big bird coming in to land drops low, slows down, and comes close to the ground. A raised wing is for flying, for display, for looking big. A lowered wing is for landing, and for covering someone.
Near the end of Ash-Shu'ara, after all the prophets' stories, the surah turns to the Prophet himself, and gives him that picture.

teach.b: The verses come in a row. First: warn your nearest kin. Bukhari reports that after this the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ climbed the hill of Safa in Mecca and called the clans of Quraysh by name.
Then, right after the warning, comes tenderness. Pickthall: "And lower thy wing (in kindness) unto those believers who follow thee."

Pickthall adds in kindness in brackets, because the Arabic picture, khafd al-janah, lowering the wing, already means it: gentleness, humility, coming down to someone's level. Notice who it's addressed to. The leader.
It's not, follow humbly. It's, lead humbly.

The Qur'an uses the same image for children and parents in Al-Isra: lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy. There the young lower the wing to the old. Here the one in charge lowers it to those who look up to him.
Either way, the person with the power to fly over others is told to come down and cover them.

And the reports of his life keep small examples: mending his own sandal, helping in his household, and telling a woman who wanted a word with him to choose any street, and he would sit with her there.
This week was a slow landing after the holy days. Six more fasts. The best ten days.
Eat, drink, remember. A calendar that moves through every season. Then back to the book: he feeds me, he heals me; bring a sound heart.

how: Muslims read 26:215 alongside the Prophet's example of humility with his companions, and many quote the parallel verse in Al-Isra about lowering the wing of humility to one's parents.

games.q: the Qur'an has just told the Prophet to warn his nearest kin. what does the very next verse tell him?
o: raise your voice so they take you seriously.
lower your wing to those who follow you.
keep your distance to keep respect.
games.why: 26:215 comes straight after the warning: lower thy wing unto those believers who follow thee.

practice: Think of someone who sees you as a little ahead of them: a younger sibling, a new colleague, a student, your own child.
Picture one ordinary moment with them, and replay it with your wing lowered: sitting at their height, listening first, asking instead of telling. If you pray, you can pray for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Khafd al-janah, lowering the wing: the Qur'an's picture of a leader coming down, like a bird landing, to cover those who follow.

orig.note: Arabic: 'and lower your wing'; janah is wing, khafd is lowering.
